title: Strip ANSI colour codes from recorded check output tails
summary: Check output tails recorded by Athena can contain ANSI escape sequences (from rustfmt etc.). Remove them in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs before the tail is cut and redacted, with unit tests; the audience is anyone reading check records.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests for stripping and run_check tail; cargo test and clippy clean.
Strip at the single point where tails are recorded rather than per tool.
Tests run a command emitting escapes and check the recorded tail.
Reuse the existing regex crate rather than add a dependency.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Second half of n5' is the recorded check tails containing rustfmt colour codes; the negative-zero cost is a separate, out-of-scope half.
Fix belongs in checks.rs run_check, where output_tail is built from raw output (line 197).
Stripping covers CSI sequences (ESC [ ... final byte), not only colour SGR.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test passes (cargo test -p athena-core) showing a string with SGR colour codes (e.g. "\x1b[31mDiff in\x1b[0m file") becomes plain text "Diff in file" via the new strip function.
A test shows run_check's output_tail for a command that prints coloured text (e.g. printf with \033[31m) contains no ESC byte (\x1b), while the raw output still drives count_tests.
Stripping happens before tail() truncation so a cut cannot leave a partial escape sequence, and plain output without escapes is unchanged.
cargo test and cargo clippy pass clean, and cargo fmt --check passes.
No new crate is added unless needed (the existing regex dependency suffices), and the change is limited to the colour-code stripping; the $-0.0000 half of n5 is untouched.

out_of_scope: The $-0.0000 negative-zero cost display (first half of n5)
Changing how checks are invoked (e.g. setting NO_COLOR)
departures: Small, well-located change; slightly higher pass odds and lower cost than reference.
